plan.title: How to Use This Sheet (Tonight: 3 Rounds, 2 Hours)
plan.body: Ye sheet tumhara kal ke exam ka master key hai. Ek hi PDF, saare 7 chapters, zero filler. Raat ko sirf teen rounds khelo - bas. Round 1 mein formulas aur tricks ratt lo (inhe padhne se hi speed aati hai). Round 2 mein har Important Question ko pehle khud try karo, phir solution se mila lo - yahi asli revision hai. Round 3 mein MCQs rapid-fire maaro aur jo galat ho, uske aage star laga do. Subah exam se pehle sirf aakhri page (Exam Morning Power Page) dobara dekho. Agar ye plan follow kiya, toh 80/80 koi badi baat nahi hai.

rounds.do: Saare Formula Tables + Concept Checklists + Speed Tricks
rounds.goal: Pura book ka hissa aankh band karke yaad ho jaye - formulas, kab-use-karna, trap warnings.
Book-style best questions with chhote solutions. Khud solve karo, phir check karo.
4 options, 1 answer, 1-line logic. Galat wale pe star - wo subah dobara dekho.
Whole book ke 12 killer formulas + exam-hall rules. Fresh dimaag = full marks.

chapters.name: Coordinate Geometry
chapters.title: Chapter 1: Coordinate Geometry
chapters.intro: Graph par points ki language: kahan hai (x, y), do points ke beech kitna faasla, midpoint kahan, reflection kaise hota hai. Formulas kam, soch smart - isi chapter mein 3-4-5 triple tumhara best friend ban jata hai.

formulas.meaning: Do points ke beech ka seedha faasla. Dono coordinates ka difference lo, square karo, jodo, root nikalo. Bas.
Point (x, y) ka ghar (origin) se faasla. Triples ratt lo: (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (8,15,17) - phir root ki zaroorat hi nahi.

formulas.f:
Same y? d = |x2 − x1|
Same x? d = |y2 − y1|
formulas.meaning: Ek coordinate same hai? Formula chhodo - bas subtract karo. Free marks!
Midpoint = dono coordinates ka average. "Bisects" dikhe toh yehi.
Ek end + midpoint diya ho toh dusra end = 2×midpoint − end. Midpoint se double karo, ek end minus.

formulas.f:
x-axis mein reflect: (x, −y)
y-axis mein reflect: (−x, y)
Origin mein: (−x, −y)
formulas.meaning: Mirror image: jis axis mein reflect karna hai, USI coordinate ka sign badlo, dusra waise hi rehne do.

formulas.f: Right angle test: (sabse badi side)<sup>2</sup> = baaki dono ka sum
formulas.meaning: Pythagoras ka ulta: agar barabar hai toh right angle confirm. Triangle type puchhe toh yehi karo.

formulas.f: Circle: point (x, y) par hai agar x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = r<sup>2</sup>
formulas.meaning: Centre origin wale circle ke liye: x<sup>2</sup>+y<sup>2</sup> chhota = andar, barabar = par, bada = bahar.

formulas.f: On the x-axis → y = 0; on the y-axis → x = 0
formulas.meaning: Axis par pade point mein dusri coordinate zero hoti hai. Equidistant point maange toh yehi maan ke solve karo.
formulas.ex: y-axis par (0, k) lo, dono points se faasla barabar rakho

formulas.f: Right triangle ka area (vertices se) = ½ × leg × leg
formulas.meaning: Right angle mil jaye toh Heron/box mat karo - dono legs multiply karke aadha. Done.

checks: Quadrant signs: I (+,+), II (−,+) - upper left, III (−,−), IV (+,−). Axis par point ho toh quadrant NAHI hota.
Ordered pair ka order matter karta hai: (3, 5) ≠ (5, 3). Pehla number x (horizontal), dusra y (vertical).
Perpendicular distance: point se x-axis ka faasla = |y|, y-axis ka = |x|. Sign nahi, magnitude.
Collinear points: teeno ke beech ka bada distance = chhote dono ka sum. Distance formula 3 baar lagao.
Parallelogram check: opposite sides equal (distance formula se) - ya diagonals ka midpoint same.
Square/rectangle verify: sides + diagonals sab check karo; square mein diagonals bhi equal hoti hain.
Rectangle ka missing vertex: opposite corners ka midpoint same hota hai - isse nikalo.
Grid-walk vs direct: galiyon mein chalna (horizontal+vertical) seedhe faasle se LAMBA hota hai, kabhi barabar nahi (except straight line).
x2+y2 compare karo r2 se - andar/par/bahar ka ek-line test.

tricks.trick: Same y? Distance = |x<sub>2</sub> - x<sub>1</sub>|. Same x? Distance = |y<sub>2</sub> - y<sub>1</sub>|
tricks.when: Points share a coordinate - skip the formula, just subtract.

tricks.trick: Distance from origin = √(x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>). Memorise triples: (3,4,5), (6,8,10), (5,12,13), (8,15,17)
tricks.when: "How far from the origin?" - spot the triple, answer in 2 seconds.

tricks.trick: Reflect in x-axis: (x, -y). In y-axis: (-x, y). In both: (-x, -y)
tricks.when: Any "mirror image / reflection" wording.

tricks.trick: Midpoint = averages of the coordinates; reverse: B = 2M - A
tricks.when: "Midpoint", "bisects", or one endpoint + midpoint given.

tricks.trick: Right angle test: (biggest side)<sup>2</sup> = sum of squares of other two
tricks.when: "Prove/verify right angle", triangle classification.

tricks.trick: Point on circle centre O radius r ⟺ x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = r<sup>2</sup>
tricks.when: "On/inside/outside the circle" - compare x<sup>2</sup>+y<sup>2</sup> with r<sup>2</sup>.

tricks.trick: "On the x-axis" → y = 0; "on the y-axis" → x = 0
tricks.when: Building coordinates of axis points.

imps.stem: A delivery boy starts at home O(0, 0), rides 4 units east to a tea stall at A(4, 0), then rides 3 units north to deliver food at B(4, 3), and finally rides straight back to O. Using the figure: (i) what is the total distance he rode? (ii) when he is at B, how far is he from home (straight line)? (iii) if a drone could fly directly from O to B, how much shorter would the O-to-B trip be compared to his road trip O-A-B?
steps: Read the figure: O to A is horizontal with the same y-coordinate, so OA = |4 - 0| = 4 units. A to B is vertical with the same x-coordinate, so AB = |3 - 0| = 3 units. Same-coordinate pairs give free distances.
The ride home B to O is the slanted stretch BO. Route makes a right angle at A, so triangle OAB has legs 4 and 3.
Distance formula (or the 3-4-5 triple): BO = √((4-0)<sup>2</sup> + (3-0)<sup>2</sup>) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5 units.
(i) Total distance ridden = OA + AB + BO = 4 + 3 + 5 = 12 units.
(ii) At B, straight-line distance from home = BO = 5 units.
(iii) Road O-A-B = 4 + 3 = 7 units; direct O-to-B = 5 units. Saving = 7 - 5 = 2 units.
why: Same-coordinate pairs need only subtraction - save the formula for the slanted side.
The right angle at A makes OB the hypotenuse - spotting the 3-4-5 triple kills the square root work instantly.
imps.hinglish: Delivery wala scene ek right triangle hai: east 4, north 3, toh ghar seedha 5 - 3-4-5 triple yaad hai na? Total ride 12 units, par seedhi line sirf 5. Graph paper par ghoomna mehnga hai, drone hi bhej do!

imps.stem: Find the distance of the point (6, 8) from the origin. Which Pythagorean triple is hiding inside this question, and how can the triple help you answer faster next time?
steps: Given: point (6, 8). Needed: distance from O(0, 0).
The hidden triple is 3-4-5 scaled by 2: 6-8-10. If you spot (6, 8), you can jump straight to 10 without squaring.
why: Spotting the triple is a safe shortcut only when BOTH numbers of a known triple appear exactly; otherwise use the formula.
imps.hinglish: Origin se distance ka short formula: √(x² + y²). 6 aur 8 ko dekhte hi 3-4-5 wala triple yaad karo - dono numbers 2 se multiply ho rahe hain, isliye answer 5 ka 2 guna = 10. Triples ratt lo: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25. Par dhyan rahe - triple tabhi use karo jab numbers EXACT match karein, warna seedha formula lagao.

imps.stem: Find the distance between A(1, 2) and B(4, 6) using (i) the helper-triangle method and (ii) the direct formula. Confirm both give the same value.
steps: Given: A(1, 2), B(4, 6). Needed: AB by two methods.
Helper triangle: the horizontal leg is |4 - 1| = 3 and the vertical leg is |6 - 2| = 4.
Both methods agree: AB = 5 units. The helper triangle simply explains where the formula comes from.
why: Showing both methods builds the habit of verifying with geometry - on hard questions this catches sign slips instantly.
imps.hinglish: Yahi chapter ka hero question hai. Helper triangle mein humne sirf differences liye - 3 aur 4 - aur wo 3-4-5 triple nikla, isliye answer 5. Formula bhi wahi karta hai, bas ek line mein. Dono ka jawab same aana hi chahiye kyunki formula Pythagoras ka hi shortcut hai. Aage se seedha formula use karo, par agar kabhi doubt ho, helper triangle bana lo.

imps.stem: The point P(4, -3) is reflected in the x-axis to get P₁, and then P₁ is reflected in the y-axis to get P₂. Write the coordinates of P₁ and P₂, and find the length PP₂.
steps: Given: P(4, -3) and a chain of two reflections. Needed: images and PP₂.
Reflection in the x-axis keeps x and flips the sign of y: P₁ = (4, 3).
Reflection in the y-axis keeps y and flips the sign of x: P₂ = (-4, 3).
Check with preserved distances: PP₁ = |3 - (-3)| = 6 (vertical segment), P₁P₂ = |(-4) - 4| = 8 (horizontal segment), and indeed 6² + 8² = 10², so the numbers are internally consistent.
imps.hinglish: Reflection ke do simple rules: x-axis mein ungli x-axis par - sirf y ka sign palto. y-axis mein - sirf x ka sign palto. Chain mein dono lagane se (4, -3) pehle (4, 3) bana, phir (-4, 3). Ab distance: 8 aur 6 ka 8-6-10 triple! Aur verification sundar hai: PP₁ = 6 vertical, P₁P₂ = 8 horizontal, inka Pythagoras bhi 10 hi deta hai. Double confirmation mil gaya.

imps.stem: A(1, 1), B(4, 1) and C(4, 5) are three points. Use the distance formula and the converse of the Baudhayana-Pythagoras Theorem to show that angle B is a right angle, and find the area of triangle ABC.
steps: Given: three vertices. Needed: prove right angle at B, then area.
Check the converse: AC² = 25 and AB² + BC² = 9 + 16 = 25. They are equal, so the angle opposite AC - which is angle B - is a right angle.
Area of a right triangle = (1/2) x leg x leg = (1/2) x 3 x 4 = 6 square units.
imps.answer: Angle B = 90 degrees (since 3² + 4² = 5² = AC²); area = 6 square units.
imps.hinglish: Converse Pythagoras ka use yaad karo: agar c² = a² + b², toh c ke saamne wala angle 90 hai. Yahan AC sabse lambi hai (5), aur 3² + 4² = 5² nikla, toh B par right angle. Area ke liye right triangle ka bonus: do legs ko base-height maan lo, (1/2)(3)(4) = 6. Coordinate geometry mein area aise hi nikalte hain jab triangle axis-aligned legs rakhta hai.

imps.stem: M(-1, 3) is the midpoint of the segment joining A(2, -4) and B(x, y). Find B, and verify your answer by checking that MA = MB.
steps: Given: midpoint and one endpoint. Needed: the other endpoint.
Solve the first: multiply by 2: -2 = 2 + x, so x = -4.
Solve the second: 6 = -4 + y, so y = 10.
Verify MB: differences (-4 - (-1)) = -3 and (10 - 3) = 7, MB = √(9 + 49) = √58. Equal, so B is correct.
why: Reverse midpoint = undo the average: multiply by 2, then subtract the known endpoint. Verification with equal distances is cheap and catches slips.
imps.hinglish: Midpoint wala equation ulta chalana hai: average diya hai, original nikalna hai. 2 se multiply karo, phir known endpoint minus karo. x ke liye: (-1)(2) - 2 = -4. y ke liye: (3)(2) - (-4) = 10. Verification zaroor karo - MA aur MB dono √58 aaye, matlab M sach mein beech mein baitha hai. Bina verification ke answer likhna adhoora hai.

imps.stem: Find the point on the y-axis that is equidistant from P(-2, 0) and Q(6, 4). Verify your answer.
steps: Given: unknown point R on the y-axis. Needed: R equidistant from P and Q.
On the y-axis the point has the form R(0, y) - fix the zero first.
Cancel y² from both sides (this is why the equation stays linear and easy): 4 = 52 - 8y.
why: Comparing squared distances avoids square roots entirely; and y² cancels, leaving a linear equation.
imps.hinglish: Y-axis par point = (0, y) - pehle yeh lock karo. Phir dono distances ke SQUARES barabar rakho, root ka jhanjhat khatam. Sabse sundar cheez: y² dono taraf cancel ho gaya aur seedha linear equation mil gaya, y = 6. Verify karo: dono distances 2√10. Aisa equidistant point technically perpendicular bisector par baithta hai - yahan humne uska sirf y-axis wala intersection nikala. 2√10 ko 6.32 likhne ki zaroorat nahi.

imps.stem: Three vertices of a rectangle are A(1, 2), B(5, 2) and C(5, 7). Find the fourth vertex D, and verify the rectangle property that its diagonals are equal.
steps: Given: three consecutive vertices. Needed: D and the diagonal check.
AB is horizontal (y = 2 for both) with length 4; BC is vertical (x = 5 for both) with length 5.
In a rectangle the fourth side DA must be vertical (above A) and CD horizontal - so D must sit directly above A at the same height as C.
Directly above A(1, 2) means x = 1; at the same height as C means y = 7. So D = (1, 7).
Verify with side lengths: DA from (1, 7) to (1, 2) has length 5, CD from (5, 7) to (1, 7) has length 4 - matching the opposite sides.
Diagonal BD = √((1 - 5)² + (7 - 2)²) = √(16 + 25) = √41. Equal, so the rectangle property holds.
imps.answer: D = (1, 7); diagonals AC = BD = √41, confirming the rectangle.
imps.hinglish: Rectangle ka chautha vertex pattern se milta hai: A ke seedha upar, C ke level par. x = 1 (A jaisa), y = 7 (C jaisa). Phir property check - diagonals barabar? Dono √41. Yahan √41 ko simplify nahi kar sakte (41 prime hai), toh root form hi final hai. Notice karo: har rectangle mein diagonals barabar hote hain - ye test humne parallelogram question (Q23) mein bhi use kiya tha, wahan fail hua tha, yahan pass.

imps.concept: Area of right triangle from coordinates (T12)
imps.stem: A triangle has vertices O(0, 0), A(8, 0) and B(0, 6). Show that it is right-angled, find its hypotenuse, and compute its area and perimeter.
steps: Given: three vertices, two of them on the axes. Needed: right angle, hypotenuse, area, perimeter.
OA lies along the x-axis: length 8. OB lies along the y-axis: length 6.
The x-axis and y-axis are perpendicular, and OA, OB lie along them, so the angle at O is 90 degrees.
Area = (1/2) x OA x OB = (1/2) x 8 x 6 = 24 square units.
Perimeter = 8 + 6 + 10 = 24 units. A charming coincidence: area 24 and perimeter 24.
imps.answer: Right angle at O; hypotenuse AB = 10; area = 24 sq units; perimeter = 24 units.
imps.hinglish: Jab triangle ke do sides axes par baithe hon, right angle free mein milta hai - axis parallel hi perpendicular hote hain. Phir 8-6-10 triple se hypotenuse 10. Area = 24, perimeter bhi 24 - dono number same! Aisi coincidences questions mein jaan-bujh ke rakhi jaati hain, toh apne practice questions mein bhi aisi numbers chuno toh checking easy hoti hai.

imps.stem: A delivery robot moves on a grid of unit squares. It must travel from station S(1, 1) to station T(7, 4). (i) What is the length of the shortest path using only horizontal and vertical moves? (ii) What is the straight-line distance? (iii) A second robot flies directly. How much distance does it save compared to the ground robot?
steps: Given: grid unit 1, S(1, 1) to T(7, 4). Needed: street length, direct length, saving.
Horizontal gap = 7 - 1 = 6 units; vertical gap = 4 - 1 = 3 units.
Ground robot (only axis moves): 6 + 3 = 9 units. Every such path has exactly this length - no order of moves can beat it.
Keep the exact answer 9 - 3√5 in the final statement; the decimal is only for intuition.
imps.hinglish: Grid-walk ka funda: horizontal steps + vertical steps hamesha fix hote hain (yahan 6 + 3 = 9), chahe kisi bhi order mein chalo. Direct distance Pythagoras se 3√5. Saving 9 - 3√5 approx 2.3 units. Ye question Q26 (city auto) ka bhai hai - wahan 200 m blocks the, yahan 1 unit. Same skeleton, naye numbers - yahi 'question structure' samajhna original practice hai, ratna nahi.

mcqs.stem: The point (-7, 4) lies in which quadrant?
mcqs.expl: x = -7 is negative and y = +4 is positive. The sign pattern (-, +) is exactly the definition of Quadrant II (above the x-axis, left of the y-axis).
mcqs.hinglish: Pehla number minus (left), doosra plus (upar) - ye Quadrant II ka signature hai. Bas signs match karo, answer mil gaya.

traps.A: (+, +) would need BOTH positive; here x is negative.
traps.C: Quadrant III is (-, -) - y must also be negative.
traps.D: Quadrant IV is (+, -) - both signs are wrong here.

mcqs.stem: The perpendicular distance of the point (-4, 9) from the y-axis is:
mcqs.expl: Distance from the y-axis is given by the size of the x-coordinate: |x| = |-4| = 4. Distances are never negative.
mcqs.hinglish: y-axis se doori = |x|. Minus sirf side batata hai (left), distance toh 4 hi hai. Distance kabhi negative nahi hota - option C khatam. √97 toh origin se distance hai (4² + 9²).

traps.A: 9 is the distance from the x-axis, not the y-axis.
traps.C: Distances are always non-negative; -4 is a coordinate, not a distance.
traps.D: √97 is the distance from the origin.

mcqs.stem: The distance between (1, -2) and (7, 6) is:
mcqs.hinglish: 6 aur 8 dikh rahe hain? 3-4-5 ka do guna - seedha 10. Triple yaad rakho toh square karne ki bhi zaroorat nahi.

traps.B: 12 would come from adding instead of applying Pythagoras.
traps.C: √84 comes from miscomputing the y-difference as 4 or 8-(-2) as something else.

mcqs.stem: If P(a, b) lies in Quadrant II, then the point (-a, -b) lies in:
mcqs.expl: In Q II, a is negative and b is positive. So -a is positive and -b is negative: signs (+, -), which is Quadrant IV. Flipping both signs reflects the point through the origin (a half-turn).
mcqs.hinglish: Q II mein a negative, b positive. Dono ke sign palte toh (+, -) = Q IV. Yaad rakho: (x, y) aur (-x, -y) hamesha opposite quadrants mein hote hain - origin ke through mirror.

traps.A: Both signs must flip, not stay one-negative-one-positive.
traps.B: Same quadrant is impossible after a half-turn.

mcqs.stem: The reflection of the point (-3, -5) in the y-axis is:
mcqs.expl: Reflection in the y-axis flips only the sign of x: (-3, -5) becomes (3, -5). The y-coordinate is untouched.
mcqs.hinglish: y-axis mein mirror = sirf x ka sign ulta. (-3, -5) ka x minus tha, ab plus: (3, -5). y ko mat chhedo - wahi sabse common galti hai.

traps.B: (3, 5) flips both signs - that is reflection in BOTH axes.
traps.C: (-3, 5) flips y only - that is the x-axis reflection.

mcqs.stem: The midpoint of the segment joining (-3, 8) and (5, -2) is:
mcqs.hinglish: Average lo dono coordinates ka: (-3 + 5)/2 = 1 aur (8 - 2)/2 = 3. (2, 6) wo galti hai jab divide karna bhool jaate ho.

traps.B: (2, 6) is the sum of the coordinates without halving.
traps.C: The y-average was computed as (8 - 2)/2 = 5 by dropping a sign.

mcqs.stem: The distance of (5, -12) from the origin is:
mcqs.expl: √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13. The 5-12-13 triple, again with a harmless minus sign.
mcqs.hinglish: 5-12-13 triple ratt lo. Minus ko ignore karo - square ke baad koi matlab nahi. 169 square hai, root nahi - aisi chhoti galti bahut log karte hain.

traps.A: 5 + (-12) size subtraction - meaningless.

mcqs.stem: The perimeter of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), (0, 3) is:
mcqs.hinglish: Axis par baithe legs 4 aur 3, hypotenuse 5. Sab JODO: 12. 7 sirf do legs ka sum hai - hypotenuse bhool gaye.

traps.A: 3 + 4 only - forgot the hypotenuse.

mcqs.stem: The area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (8, 0) and (0, 6) is:
mcqs.expl: Right angle at the origin with legs 8 and 6. Area = (1/2)(8)(6) = 24.
mcqs.hinglish: Right triangle ka area = aadha x base x height = 24. 48 wo galti hai jab 1/2 multiply karna bhool jaate ho.

traps.A: Missing the factor 1/2.

mcqs.stem: Assertion (A): The distance of a point (x, y) from the origin is √(x² + y²). Reason (R): The Baudhayana-Pythagoras Theorem gives hypotenuse = √(sum of squares of legs). Choose the correct option:
options: Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true
mcqs.expl: The distance formula from the origin is exactly Pythagoras applied to the legs x and y. The assertion is true and the reason is the actual justification behind it.
mcqs.hinglish: A sahi hai, aur wo sahi ISLIYE hai kyunki origin se jaane wala segment right triangle ka hypotenuse hai jiske legs x aur y hain. R wahi theorem hai - toh R, A ko explain karta hai. Option A.

traps.B: R genuinely explains A here - do not dismiss the connection.
traps.C: R is a correct statement of the theorem.
traps.D: A is the standard distance-from-origin result.

mcqs.stem: The point (x, 0) is equidistant from (2, 3) and (6, 3). Then x equals:
mcqs.expl: (x - 2)² + 9 = (x - 6)² + 9. The 9s cancel: (x - 2)² = (x - 6)², so x - 2 = plus/minus (x - 6). The negative-sign branch gives a contradiction (0 = -8... no solution from that branch), the positive-sign branch gives x - 2 = x - 6? Also impossible - so take x - 2 = -(x - 6): 2x = 8, x = 4. Geometrically, x = 4 is the midpoint of 2 and 6, directly below the midpoint of the two given points.
mcqs.hinglish: Dono given points ka y same hai (3), isliye equidistant point unke beech ke THEEK beech mein hoga: (2 + 6)/2 = 4. Equation se bhi x = 4 hi aata hai. Ye symmetry ka use hai - jab dono points same height par hon toh answer unka midpoint hota hai.

traps.B: That is the first point itself.
traps.C: 8 is beyond the second point - not symmetric.
traps.D: 3 is not the average of 2 and 6.

mcqs.stem: Statement: If the two points in a distance calculation are interchanged, the computed distance changes. Is the statement TRUE or FALSE, and why?
options: TRUE, because x and y swap places
FALSE, because the differences are squared, which erases the sign change
TRUE, because the formula is order-dependent
FALSE, because distance is always zero
mcqs.expl: Swapping the points changes (x2 - x1) into (x1 - x2) = negative of it. But squaring makes both equal. Hence the distance is unchanged.
mcqs.hinglish: Points ulta karne se differences ka sign ulta hota hai, par square laga-te-hi sign khatam. Isliye distance same rehta hai. Ye freedom hai - jis point ko pehle maano, jawab same.

traps.A: Coordinates do not swap - only the subtraction order flips.
traps.D: Distance is zero only for identical points.

mcqs.stem: A point whose x-coordinate is 0 must lie:
mcqs.expl: x = 0 means zero sideways distance from the y-axis, so the point sits on the y-axis - at (0, y) for some y. It is the origin only if additionally y = 0.
mcqs.hinglish: x = 0 matlab left-right displacement zero = seedha y-axis par. Origin tabhi banega jab y bhi 0 ho. x-axis wale options mein y = 0 hota hai - ulta mat karo.

traps.A: On the x-axis it is y that equals 0.
traps.C: Quadrant points have both coordinates non-zero.

mcqs.stem: For the right triangle with vertices (0, 0), (6, 0) and (0, 8), the point equidistant from all three vertices is:
mcqs.expl: Hypotenuse joins (6, 0) to (0, 8); its midpoint is (3, 4). In a right triangle the midpoint of the hypotenuse is equidistant from all three vertices (distance 5 here: 3-4-5 again).
mcqs.hinglish: Q42 wala theorem yaad karo - right triangle mein hypotenuse ka MIDPOINT hi teeno se equidistant. (6,0) aur (0,8) ka midpoint = (3, 4). Distance check: origin se 5, dono vertices se 5. Bang on.

traps.B: Not the midpoint of the hypotenuse.

chapters.name: Linear Equations in One and Two Variables
chapters.title: Chapter 2: Linear Equations in One and Two Variables
chapters.intro: Duniya ke har "fixed + per-unit" scene ko ek line y = ax + b mein likhna. Bill ho, age ho, tanki ho ya matchstick pattern - sab isi ek shape mein aata hai. Slope aur intercept padhna seekh lo, chapter khatam.

formulas.meaning: a = har unit ka rate (slope), b = shuruati/fixed amount. "Rs 300 joining + Rs 60 per session" → y = 60x + 300.
Per step kitna badla. Upar utha toh plus, neeche gira toh minus.

formulas.f: Do bills diya ho? Equations MINUS karo
formulas.meaning: Dono equations ko subtract karo - fixed wala (b) cancel ho jata hai, rate (a) khud nikal aata hai. Phir b wapas nikaalo.
formulas.ex: y = ax + b ke 2 points → pehle a, phir b

formulas.f: Pattern: T(n) = kn + c, jahan c = (first term) − k
formulas.meaning: Har step mein utna hi add ho (k)? Toh linear pattern. c nikaalne ke liye pehle term se k ghatao.

formulas.f: y-intercept = (0, b); x-intercept: y = 0 rakh ke solve
formulas.meaning: Line jahan y-axis ko kaate = (0, b). x-axis ka point chahiye toh y ko zero maan lo.

formulas.f: Bada |a| = steeper line; same a = parallel lines
formulas.meaning: Slope compare karo: jiska |a| bada, wo zyada khadi. a same ho toh kabhi milengi nahi (parallel).
Scene padho: paisa jud raha hai toh slope plus, fat raha hai toh minus. Decay mein bhi formula same.

formulas.f: p(x) ki value: x ki jagah number daal do
formulas.meaning: Polynomial machine hai - input daalo, output lo. p(x) = 3x − 7 at x = 5: 15 − 7 = 8.
2x + 9 linear, x<sup>2</sup> + 1 quadratic, x<sup>3</sup> cubic. Constant polynomial ka degree 0.

checks: Variable pehchano: jo cheez badal rahi hai (sessions, km, months) wahi x hai; jo puchha hai wo y.
Fixed fee kabhi x se multiply nahi hoti - wo b hai, chahe kuch bhi ho.
Do conditions = do equations. "Sum 50 aur difference 8" jaise scenes minus/karne par solve hote hain.
Age problems: "Mother 4 times daughter" → m = 4d; saalon baad dono mein +k add hota hai.
Coin/money problems: count alag, value alag - 5x + 10y type equation banao.
Matchstick patterns: pehla figure alag (c), har naya figure fixed adds (k) → T(n) = kn + c.
Line ki graph reading: (0, b) se shuru, slope a se chadho/utro. Har point (x, y) line par hai agar equation satisfy ho.
Two lines same equation = same line (infinite solutions); same a different b = parallel (no meeting).
C ≠ F kabhi barabar nahi hota? Hota hai! F = 1.8C + 32 mein C = F rakho: C = −40. Yaad rakhna, HOTS favourite.

tricks.trick: Fixed fee + rate × quantity → y = ax + b (b = fixed part, a = per-unit rate)
tricks.when: "Rs 300 joining + Rs 60 per session" style wording.

tricks.when: Fit y = ax + b from two bills or data points.

tricks.when: Matchstick, tile and money patterns.

imps.stem: The sum of two numbers is 50, and one of them is 8 more than the other. Find the numbers.
steps: Let the smaller number be x. Then the larger is x + 8.
Check in words: 21 + 29 = 50 and 29 - 21 = 8. Both conditions hold.
imps.hinglish: Chota number x maan lo, bada apne aap x + 8 ban jaata hai. Sum equation se x = 21. Aur LAST STEP yaad rakho: dono numbers report karo - sirf 'x = 21' likha toh aadha answer hai. Words mein wapas check karo, equation mein hi nahi.

imps.stem: A badminton academy charges a joining fee of Rs 300 plus Rs 60 for every session attended. (i) Write the total cost for n sessions. (ii) Find the cost for 12 sessions. (iii) A player paid Rs 780 in total. How many sessions did she attend?
imps.hinglish: Fixed + rate x count - yahi har bill ka formula hai. Aage jaane ke liye substitute, peeche aane ke liye solve. 780 mein se 300 hataya toh sessions ka khel bacha: 480/60 = 8.

imps.stem: Bela has Rs 500 and spends Rs 30 every day. (i) Write the amount left after n days. (ii) After how many days will she be left with Rs 200? (iii) What is the amount left after 15 days, and why does the model stay valid only up to 10 days of reaching zero? Actually find the exact day her money runs out.
steps: Running out: 500 - 30n = 0 gives n = 500/30 = 16.67 days. Money reaches zero partway through the 17th day.
So the linear model describes her cash only until about 16.67 days; beyond that the amount cannot go below 0.
imps.answer: (i) 500 - 30n (ii) after 10 days (iii) Rs 50 after 15 days; money hits zero during the 17th day (n = 500/30 = 16.67), where the model ends.
why: Real decay models hit a floor. Reporting WHEN the floor is reached (and that the model stops there) is the mark of a careful modeller.
imps.hinglish: Decay question mein teen sawaal hote hain: kitna bacha (substitute), kab itna bacha (solve), kab khatam (zero set karo). Yahan 16.67 din - matlab 17ve din ke beech mein khatam. Model ki limit batana bhi answer ka hissa hai - paisa negative nahi ho sakta!

imps.stem: A taxi charges Rs 40 for the first 3 km (and any part of it), then Rs 18 for every additional km. (i) Find the fare for a 12 km trip. (ii) Write the fare for a trip of n km where n is at least 3. (iii) For what distance is the fare Rs 148?
steps: Beyond 3 km, chargeable extra distance = (n - 3) km.
General: F(n) = 40 + 18(n - 3) = 18n - 54 + 40 = 18n - 14, valid for n at least 3.
Check with the original description: 40 for the first 3 km plus 18 x 6 = 108 for the next 6 km: total 148. Correct.
imps.answer: (i) Rs 202 (ii) F(n) = 18n - 14 for n at least 3 (iii) 9 km.
imps.hinglish: PDF ke auto-fare jaisa hi question, bas numbers naye. Formula banane ke liye (n - 3) ka idea zaroori hai - pehle 3 km ka paisa already fixed 40 mein hai. Simplify karke 18n - 14 milta hai aur reverse solve se 9 km. Hamesha original description se verify karo.

imps.stem: A mother is 4 times as old as her daughter. After 6 years, the sum of their ages will be 82 years. Find their present ages.
steps: Let the daughter be x now; the mother is 4x.
Check: after 6 years they are 20 and 62, sum 82. Correct.
imps.hinglish: Age questions mein 'after' ka matlab dono ke age mein addition. 5x + 12 = 82 se x = 14. Check zaroori: 20 + 62 = 82. Mother 4x isliye 56 - equation se nahi, definition se.

imps.stem: A learning platform charges a fixed monthly fee plus a per-module charge. A student observed that accessing 10 modules cost Rs 400 and accessing 14 modules cost Rs 500. Assuming the bill is y = ax + b, find a and b, and interpret both numbers.
steps: Substitute both observations into y = ax + b: 400 = 10a + b and 500 = 14a + b.
Subtract the first from the second: 100 = 4a, so a = 25.
Back-substitute into the first: 400 = 10(25) + b = 250 + b, so b = 150.
Interpretation: a = 25 is the charge per module (Rs 25 per module); b = 150 is the fixed monthly fee (Rs 150 even with zero modules).
Verify with the second point: 25(14) + 150 = 350 + 150 = 500. Correct.
why: Subtracting the equations kills b instantly - the entire technique rests on b being identical in both lines.
imps.hinglish: Do observation, do equation, ek SUBTRACTION - b khatam, a seedha mil gaya (25). Phir wapas jao, b nikaalo (150). Interpretation zaroor likho: 25 = per-module charge, 150 = fixed fee. Ye interpretation wali line hi examiner ko dikhati hai ki tumne samjha hai, sirf calculation nahi kiya.

imps.stem: The relation between Celsius C and Fahrenheit F has the linear form F = aC + b. Water melts at 0 degrees Celsius and 32 degrees Fahrenheit, and boils at 100 degrees Celsius and 212 degrees Fahrenheit. Find a and b.
steps: First data point: C = 0, F = 32 gives 32 = a(0) + b, so b = 32 directly - a gift.
Second data point: C = 100, F = 212 gives 212 = 100a + 32.
The relation is F = 1.8C + 32, the famous conversion formula.
imps.hinglish: Yahan data ki kripa se b PEHLE mil gaya (zero input pe output hi b hai!). Phir sirf ek equation bachi, a = 1.8. Ye formula tum pehle se jaante ho - ab tumne use DERIVE kiya hai. Fitting ka asli maza yahi hai.

imps.stem: Squares are made with matchsticks placed in a row, each new square sharing one side with the previous one. The counts are 4, 7, 10, ... (i) How many matchsticks for n squares? (ii) For 22 squares? (iii) Can exactly 100 matchsticks form such a row of squares? Justify.
steps: Sequence 4, 7, 10 has constant difference 3: rule M(n) = 3n + c. From stage 1: 3 + c = 4, so c = 1. Rule: M(n) = 3n + 1.
n = 33 is a whole number, so YES - a row of 33 squares uses exactly 100 matchsticks.
The justification is the integrality of n: patterns exist only at whole-number stages.
imps.answer: (i) 3n + 1 (ii) 67 (iii) Yes - stage n = 33 uses exactly 100 matchsticks.
imps.hinglish: 3n + 1 wala rule - ek square 4, har naya square sirf 3 extra le raha hai kyunki ek side share hoti hai. 'Can 100 form a stage?' ka matlab: solve karo aur INTEGRITY check karo. Yahan n = 33 whole number - YES. Agar 33.33 aata toh answer 'No, kabhi nahi' hota - aur wahi asli answer hota.

imps.stem: Draw-free reasoning: compare the graphs of y = 3x + 1 and y = -3x + 1. State their common features, their differences, and the geometric relationship between the two lines.
steps: Common feature: same b = 1, so both cut the y-axis at the same point (0, 1).
Difference: slopes +3 and -3 - equal in size, opposite in sign.
Positive slope: as x grows, y grows (uphill). Negative slope: as x grows, y falls (downhill).
Geometric relationship: the two lines are mirror images of each other in the y-axis. Reason: replacing x by -x in y = 3x + 1 gives y = -3x + 1 - reflection in the y-axis flips the sign of x.
They are NOT parallel (slopes differ), so they cross - exactly at the shared point (0, 1).
imps.answer: Both pass through (0, 1); slopes +3 and -3 make them mirror images in the y-axis, crossing at (0, 1) - not parallel.
imps.hinglish: Same intercept, opposite slopes: dono lines (0, 1) mein milti hain aur wahan se ek upar, ek neeche jaati hain - y-axis ke aaine mein twin. 'Replace x by -x' wala reflection argument coordinate geometry ka classic move hai - Chapter 1 ke reflections se seedha connection.

imps.stem: A wire of length 36 cm is bent into a rectangle. Let the length be x cm. (i) Write the area as a function of x. (ii) Find ALL lengths x that give an area of 77 sq cm. (iii) Which single length gives the largest area, and what is that area?
steps: Perimeter 36 means half-perimeter 18: length + width = 18. Width = 18 - x.
Area A(x) = x(18 - x) = 18x - x² - a quadratic function (the PDF builds exactly this in its Example 3 with a 20 cm wire).
Set x(18 - x) = 77: x² - 18x + 77 = 0. Look for two numbers with product 77 and sum 18: 7 and 11.
So x = 7 or x = 11. Both are genuine: a 7 x 11 rectangle and an 11 x 7 rectangle are the SAME rectangle turned around - one answer in two descriptions.
Largest area: test symmetric candidates. x = 9 gives 9 x 9 = 81; x = 8 gives 8 x 10 = 80; x = 10 gives 10 x 8 = 80. The square (x = 9) wins with area 81.
Structure noticed: areas rise toward x = 9 and fall after it - symmetric about the square.
imps.answer: (i) A(x) = 18x - x² (ii) x = 7 or 11 (the same rectangle, two descriptions) (iii) x = 9 gives the maximum area 81 sq cm.
imps.hinglish: Ye PDF ke wire example ka bada bhai. Area quadratic nikla (18x - x²) - chapter linear hai par evaluation quadratic ki bhi practice hai (Ex 2.2 mein tha). 77 ke liye do answers (7 aur 11) ek hi rectangle ke do naam hain - symmetry! Aur square (9 x 9 = 81) max deta hai - ye observation Grade 10 mein formally aayega, aaj ke liye table-test kaafi hai.

mcqs.stem: The coefficient of x in the expression 5x - 7 is:
mcqs.expl: The coefficient is the number multiplying the variable x, which is 5. The -7 is the constant term.
mcqs.hinglish: Coefficient = variable ke saath juda number. 5x ka coefficient 5. -7 constant hai, coefficient nahi.

traps.B: -7 is the constant term, not attached to x.
traps.D: 1 is the coefficient of a bare x, not of 5x.

mcqs.stem: The degree of the polynomial 4 - 3y + y² is:
mcqs.expl: The powers present are 0 (the 4), 1 (the -3y) and 2 (the y²). The highest is 2, so the degree is 2.
mcqs.hinglish: Order mein likha nahi hai par koi baat nahi - powers scan karo: 0, 1, 2. Max = 2. Quadratic.

traps.A: 1 is just the middle term's power.

mcqs.stem: The degree of the constant polynomial -9 is:
mcqs.expl: Any constant c can be written as c x x⁰, and x⁰ = 1. So the degree (power of the variable) is 0.
mcqs.hinglish: Constant ka degree ZERO hota hai - isko x⁰ ke roop mein likh sakte ho. Ye MCQ ka pakka sawaal hai.

traps.A: -9 is the value, not the degree.
traps.C: There is no x term at all.

mcqs.stem: The value of 4x - 9 at x = -2 is:
mcqs.hinglish: 4(-2) = -8, phir -9 jodo: -17. Dono negative milke aur negative - sign ka khel.

mcqs.stem: The machine y = 5x + 2 gives output 27. The input x is:
mcqs.hinglish: Peeche chalna hai: 27 se 2 ghatayo (25), 5 se divide (5). Verify: 5(5) + 2 = 27.

mcqs.stem: Two numbers add to 46, and one of them is 6 more than the other. The numbers are:
mcqs.expl: Let them be x and x + 6: 2x + 6 = 46 gives x = 20. Numbers 20 and 26.
mcqs.hinglish: 2x + 6 = 46 se x = 20. Check: 20 + 26 = 46, difference 6. Dono condition sahi.

mcqs.stem: A sequence begins 4, 9, 14, 19, ... Its nth-term rule is:
mcqs.expl: The constant difference is 5, so the rule is 5n + c. Stage 1: 5 + c = 4 gives c = -1. Rule: 5n - 1. Check stage 2: 10 - 1 = 9. Correct.
mcqs.hinglish: Difference 5 pakdo, phir first term se c nikaalo: 4 = 5 + c isliye c = -1. 5n - 1. Verify with 9: 10 - 1 = 9 sahi.

traps.B: Would give 6 as the first term.

mcqs.stem: A service costs Rs 90 for 2 units and Rs 210 for 6 units. In the model y = ax + b:
mcqs.hinglish: 4 units ka difference 120: per-unit 30. Wapas: 90 - 60 = 30 fixed. Interpretation: Rs 30 per unit + Rs 30 base.

traps.B: Forgot to subtract the per-unit part.
traps.C: Mixed up which pair to use.

mcqs.stem: In the conversion F = 1.8C + 32, the number 1.8 tells us that:
options: a 1 degree rise in Celsius gives a 1.8 degree rise in Fahrenheit
Fahrenheit is always 1.8 more than Celsius
mcqs.expl: The slope is the rate of change: each extra degree Celsius lifts the Fahrenheit reading by 1.8. (Option B confuses slope with a constant offset - the offset is 32, not 1.8.)
mcqs.hinglish: Slope = rate: C mein 1 degree badho toh F mein 1.8 badho. Fixed gap toh 32 hai - wo b wala hissa hai, 1.8 nahi.

traps.B: That is what b would mean, but b = 32 here.

mcqs.stem: The slope of the line 3y = 6x + 12 is:
mcqs.expl: Divide by 3 first: y = 2x + 4. The slope is 2. Reading the raw coefficient 6 before isolating y is the classic trap.
mcqs.hinglish: Pehle y = ... banao! 3 se divide: y = 2x + 4. Slope 2. Seedha 6 padhna sabse common galti hai.

traps.A: That is the coefficient of x before dividing.
traps.D: That is the constant after dividing.

mcqs.stem: Which of these lines passes through the origin?
mcqs.expl: A line passes through (0, 0) exactly when its constant term b is 0. Only y = 5x has b = 0.
mcqs.hinglish: Origin se guzarne ka ek hi test: b = 0. Baaki sab (0, b) par y-axis kaat-ti hain, origin se nahi.

mcqs.stem: The lines y = 4x - 3 and y = 4x + 7 are:
mcqs.expl: Same slope 4, different intercepts (-3 vs 7): parallel lines that never meet.
mcqs.hinglish: Slope same, intercept alag = parallel. Same slope SAME intercept hota toh ek hi line hoti.

traps.A: Perpendicularity is about slope products -1, not equality.

mcqs.stem: The model h(t) = 3 - 0.5t describes:
mcqs.expl: The rate of change (slope) is -0.5: each month the height drops by 0.5. Negative slope means decay.
mcqs.hinglish: Slope negative = decay. 3 starting value, 0.5 per month girawat - PDF ke water-tank example jaisa.

traps.A: Growth needs a positive slope.
traps.C: Something IS changing - by 0.5 per step.

mcqs.stem: The line y = 3x + 6 and the two coordinate axes form a triangle. Its area is:
mcqs.expl: y-intercept (0, 6); x-intercept: 3x + 6 = 0 gives x = -2, point (-2, 0). Right triangle with legs 6 and 2: area = (1/2)(6)(2) = 6.
mcqs.hinglish: Intercepts (0, 6) aur (-2, 0). Origin ke saath right triangle: legs 6 aur 2, area 6. Length absolute value mein lo - negative coordinate se area negative nahi hota.

chapters.name: Number Systems and Exponents
chapters.title: Chapter 3: Number Systems and Exponents
chapters.intro: Numbers ki family tree (N, Z, Q, R), recurring decimals ko fraction banana, surds ko rationalise karna aur exponent laws. Proof wale questions (√2, √3, √5 irrational) pakke aate hain - skeleton ratt lo.

formulas.meaning: Counting numbers → unme negatives jude → unme fractions jude → unme irrationals jude. Har naya set purana cover karta hai.
formulas.ex: −3 ∈ Z, 2/7 ∈ Q, √2 ∈ R par Q se bahar

formulas.f: Terminating test: fraction ko REDUCE karo, denominator sirf 2<sup>m</sup> × 5<sup>n</sup> ho toh terminate
formulas.meaning: Pehle simplify karo (33/125 → already clean), phir denominator ke prime factors dekho. 3, 7, 11 aaye = non-terminating repeating.
Jitne digits repeat, utne 9s denominator mein. 0.777... = 7/9; 0.454545... = 45/99 = 5/11.
Upar: poori decimal ke digits minus jo pehle the. Neeche: 9s (repeating ke liye) + 0s (non-repeating ke liye).
Same root ke surds multiply/divide ho toh andar jodo/kaato. Pehle simplify karna best: √72 = 6√2.
Neeche √a ± √b ho toh (√a ± √b) se upar-neeche multiply - (a−b) formula se root gayab.

formulas.f: a<sup>m</sup> × a<sup>n</sup> = a<sup>m+n</sup>; a<sup>m</sup>/a<sup>n</sup> = a<sup>m−n</sup>; (a<sup>m</sup>)<sup>n</sup> = a<sup>mn</sup>
formulas.meaning: Multiply = powers add; divide = powers minus; power of power = powers multiply. Base SAME hona chahiye.
Zero power = 1. Minus power = palat do. Fraction power = root. 64<sup>2/3</sup> matlab cube root of 64, phir square.

formulas.f: Same base banao → exponents barabar rakh do
formulas.meaning: 8 = 2<sup>3</sup>, 125 = 5<sup>3</sup>, 1/81 = 3<sup>−4</sup>. Dono side same base aaye toh powers equate karo - equation solved.

formulas.f: rational ± irrational = irrational; irrational × non-zero rational = irrational
formulas.meaning: Ek irrational ke saath rational jodo ya guna karo - result irrational hi rahega (rational × rational ke alawa).

checks: Irrational ka matlab: decimal na terminate ho, na repeat. √2, π, 0.101001000... sab irrational.
0.999... = 1 exactly - proof: x = 0.999..., 10x = 9.999..., 10x − x = 9 → x = 1. MCQ favourite!
Between any two rationals infinitely many irrationals (aur vice versa) - density. Example banane ke liye surds use karo: √(a/b) forms.
√n irrational jab tak n perfect square na ho - 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 sabke roots irrational; √4, √9, √16 rational.
Irrationality proof ka skeleton: maan lo p/q (lowest terms) → square karo → prime p, q ko divide karta hai → p, q dono divide karte hain → contradiction. Iska flow ratt lo.
Compare surds: sabko same root ke andar le aao - (√7)2 = 7, (2√2)2 = 8, (3)2 = 9 → order mil gaya.
Conjugate pair magic: x = 2 + √3 ho toh 1/x = 2 − √3 (multiply karke check karo). x ± 1/x ke questions isi se khul te hain.
Telescoping sum: 1/(√2+1) + 1/(√3+√2) + ... har term rationalise karne par √(next) − √(prev) bachta hai - chain collapse ho jati hai.
Nested radical: √(7 + 4√3) = √(4 + 3 + 2·2·√3) = 2 + √3. Pattern: m + n = given, mn = inner term.

tricks.trick: Terminating? REDUCE first, then check: denominator = 2<sup>m</sup> × 5<sup>n</sup> only
tricks.when: "Without long division, state whether the decimal terminates".

tricks.trick: Pure recurring 0.abab... = block/99...9. Mixed: (all digits - non-repeating)/99..900..0
tricks.when: Convert recurring decimals to p/q form.

tricks.trick: Compare surds: same root index banao, then compare inside values
tricks.when: "Arrange in increasing order".

tricks.trick: Rationalise: multiply by the conjugate. Telescoping sum collapses to (last - first)
tricks.when: Surds in denominators; 1/(√a+√b) chains.

tricks.trick: Same base first: 8 = 2<sup>3</sup>, 125 = 5<sup>3</sup>, 1/81 = 3<sup>-4</sup> → equate exponents
tricks.when: Every exponent equation.

tricks.trick: Irrationality skeleton: assume p/q → square → prime lemma → contradiction
tricks.when: "Prove √2 / √3 / √5 is irrational".

tricks.trick: rational ± irrational = irrational; irrational × non-zero rational = irrational
tricks.when: True/false closure statements.

imps.stem: Without performing long division, decide whether each decimal expansion terminates: (i) 17/8, (ii) 13/3125, (iii) 7/12, (iv) 64/455, (v) 6/15.
steps: Given: five fractions. Needed: terminating or not, via the 2ᵐ × 5ⁿ test on the REDUCED denominator.
(iii) 7/12: 12 = 2² × 3. The stray 3 can never be absorbed into a power of 10, so it recurs.
(iv) 64/455: 455 = 5 × 7 × 13. The primes 7 and 13 force a recurring decimal.
(v) 6/15: reduce first! 6/15 = 2/5, and 5 = 5¹, so it terminates (0.4). Testing 15 = 3 × 5 without reducing would give the wrong verdict.
why: 10 = 2 × 5, so a fraction terminates exactly when its reduced denominator divides some power of 10 - only primes 2 and 5 can appear.
imps.hinglish: Sabse pehla kaam: fraction ko lowest terms mein lao. Phir denominator ko prime factors mein todo. Sirf 2 aur 5 dikh rahe hain? Decimal ruk jayega. Koi aur prime (3, 7, 13...) dikh gaya? Chalti-firti decimal aayegi. (v) wala question isliye diya hai kyunki students 15 dekh ke turant 'recur' bol dete hain - pehle 3 cancel karo!

imps.stem: Express in p/q form: (i) 0.777... (the 7 repeating), (ii) 0.373737... (the block 37 repeating), (iii) 0.090909... (the block 09 repeating).
steps: Given: three pure recurring decimals (repeat starts immediately). Needed: exact fractions.
(i) Let x = 0.777... . Multiply by 10 (one repeating digit → shift by one place): 10x = 7.777... .
(ii) Let x = 0.373737... . Two repeating digits → multiply by 100: 100x = 37.3737... .
(iii) Let x = 0.090909... . Two repeating digits → 100x = 9.0909... . Subtract: 99x = 9, x = 9/99 = 1/11.
why: Multiplying by 10ᵋ lines up two identical infinite tails; subtracting cancels them and leaves a finite equation. k repeating digits need a shift of 10ᵋ.
imps.hinglish: Rule simple hai: jitne digit repeat ho rahe hain, utne 9 denominator mein. Ek digit repeat = 9, do digit = 99. 0.777... = 7/9, 0.3737... = 37/99. Bas repeating block ke digits upar likh do aur neeche utne hi 9. (iii) mein 9/99 ko 1/11 tak reduce karna mat bhoolna.

imps.stem: Simplify into k√( ) form: (i) √72, (ii) √245, (iii) √175, (iv) √(147).
steps: Given: four radicals. Needed: extract every perfect-square factor.
why: √(ab) = √a√b lets the perfect-square factor walk out of the root; what remains inside must be square-free.
imps.hinglish: Andar sabse bada perfect square dhoondo aur bahar nikalo. 72 = 36×2, 36 ka root 6, toh 6√2. Yaad rakho: 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100, 121, 144 - ye aapke dost hain. Jitna bada square nikaloge, utna chhota root; 72 ko 4×18 karke √18 ko phir simplify karna double kaam hai.

imps.stem: Prove that √3 is irrational.
steps: Given: a claim to contradict. Assume √3 = p/q where p, q are integers, q ≠ 0, and the fraction is in lowest terms (p and q share no common prime).
Squaring both sides: 3 = p²/q², so p² = 3q².
Then 3 divides p². Since 3 is prime, 3 divides p itself (a prime dividing a square must divide the number). Write p = 3r.
So 3 divides q², hence 3 divides q.
Now 3 divides both p and q - contradicting lowest terms. The assumption is false, therefore √3 is irrational. ∎
imps.answer: √3 is irrational (by contradiction; 3 divides both p and q, contradicting lowest terms).
why: The contradiction must land on the EXACT assumption made (coprimality); that is why the final sentence names lowest terms.
imps.hinglish: Proof ka 4-step skeleton yaad karo: (1) assume p/q lowest terms, (2) square karo - prime upar aa jata hai, (3) prime dono (p aur q) ko divide karta nikla, (4) lowest terms se contradiction - done! √2 mein prime 2 tha, yahan 3 hai, √5 mein 5 hoga. Bas prime badlo, skeleton same.

imps.stem: Rationalise the denominator and simplify: 1/(3 + 2√2).
steps: Given: denominator 3 + 2√2. Its conjugate is 3 - 2√2 (flip the sign of the surd term).
Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate:
So the expression equals 3 - 2√2. Check numerically: 1/(3 + 2.828...) = 1/5.828... ≈ 0.1716, and 3 - 2.828... = 0.1716 ✓.
why: The conjugate turns the denominator into a² - b², which has no surds; here it even collapses to 1, giving a free simplification.
imps.hinglish: Conjugate ka matlab: sirf beech ka sign ulta. 3 + 2√2 ka conjugate 3 - 2√2. Multiply karo, denominator (a+b)(a-b) = a²-b² ban jata hai. Yahan 9-8=1 nikla - jackpot! Answer 3-2√2. Aise lucky cases (denominator 1) exam mein bahut aate hain, isliye denominator ko poori tarah simplify karna kabhi mat chhodna.

imps.stem: Arrange in increasing order: √7, 2√2, √5, 3√3/2.
steps: Given: four positive surds. All are positive, so squaring preserves the order.
why: For positive quantities a < b ⇔ a² < b² - comparing squares avoids fiddly decimal roots.
imps.hinglish: Compare karne ka best trick: dono ko square karo. 2√2 ka square (2)² × 2 = 8 hota hai - coefficient bhi square hota hai, ye bhoolna sabse common galti hai! (3√3/2)² = 9×3/4 = 6.75. Ab squares ko order karo aur original order likho. Numerical check se confirm kar lo.

steps: Given: three exponential equations. Strategy: one base on both sides, then equate exponents.
why: Equality of powers with the same base forces equal exponents; the whole game is rewriting both sides into one base.
imps.hinglish: Exponent equation mein dono taraf SAME base lao. 1/81 ko 3⁻⁴ dekho - negative exponent ka perfect use. (2/3)ˣ = 27/8 mein ulta fraction banana padta hai: 27/8 = (3/2)³ = (2/3)⁻³. Fraction ka negative exponent = fraction flip. Ye teen patterns exam ke favourites hain.

imps.stem: Evaluate without a calculator: (i) (81/16)⁻³⁴ʸ... rewrite: (81/16)^(-3/4), (ii) 8^(2/3) + 4^(-1/2), (iii) (5²/√5)².
steps: Given: expressions with fractional and negative exponents.
(i) (81/16)^(-3/4): the negative exponent flips the fraction; the 1/4 takes a fourth root. (16/81)^(3/4) = (⁴√(16/81))³ = (2/3)³ = 8/27.
why: a^(m/n) = (root n of a) to the m; the negative sign means reciprocal. Order root-then-power keeps numbers small.
imps.hinglish: Fractional exponent do kaam karta hai: neeche wala number ROOT, upar wala POWER. 8^(2/3): cube root of 8 = 2, phir square = 4. Negative exponent: flip karo. Root pehle lo, power baad mein - numbers chhote rehte hain. (i) mein (81/16) ko flip karke 16/81 banana zaroori tha.

imps.stem: If x = 2 + √3, find the value of x² + 1/x² without evaluating x numerically beyond the given form.
steps: So x and 1/x are conjugates: x = 2 + √3, 1/x = 2 - √3.
why: Conjugate reciprocals have surd terms in opposite signs; squares keep that symmetry, so the middle terms cancel on adding.
imps.hinglish: Ye conjugate-pair trick poore algebra mein chalega. Pehle 1/x nikaalo - denominator 1 aaya, matlab x aur 1/x perfect conjugates. Square karke jodo: ±4√3 terms aapas mein uda do. Answer 14. Aage ke liye yaad rakho: x³ + 1/x³ = (x + 1/x)³ - 3(x + 1/x).

steps: Key identity: 1/(√(n+1) + √n) = √(n+1) - √n (multiply by the conjugate; denominator becomes n+1-n = 1).
why: Each conjugate-rationalised term is a difference of consecutive roots; in the written sum every middle root appears once with plus and once with minus.
imps.hinglish: Ye 'telescoping' pattern dekho: har term rationalise karne par root ka difference banta hai: √2-1, √3-√2, 2-√3. Jodne par beech ke saare roots gayab, sirf first ka minus aur last ka plus bachta hai: 2 - 1 = 1. Agar 1/(√(n+1)+√n) type dikhe, turant conjugate socho.

mcqs.stem: Which of the following is irrational?
mcqs.expl: The gaps between 1s keep growing, so no block repeats: non-terminating, non-recurring, hence irrational. The others terminate or simplify (0.25, 3/8, √49 = 7).
mcqs.hinglish: Pattern dekho - ones ke beech gap badhta ja raha hai, koi block repeat nahi hoga. Isliye irrational. Baaki teeno rational hain.

mcqs.stem: 0.333... (the 3 repeating) written as a fraction is:
mcqs.hinglish: Ek digit repeat = upar wo digit, neeche 9. 3/9 = 1/3. Denominator 10 wale options terminating decimals dete hain - wo galat.

mcqs.stem: Without division, the decimal expansion of 77/210 is:
mcqs.expl: 77/210 = 11/30 (cancel 7). 30 = 2 × 3 × 5 has the prime 3, so it recurs.
mcqs.hinglish: Pehle 7 cancel karo - 11/30 banta hai. 30 mein 3 hai, toh recurring. Ye reduce-first wala hi case hai.

traps.A: 30 is not of the form 2ᵐ×5ⁿ.
traps.C: Every rational recurs or terminates - never truly random.

mcqs.stem: Which statement is TRUE?
mcqs.expl: Naturals sit inside integers, integers inside rationals, rationals inside reals: N ⊂ Z ⊂ Q ⊂ R. So N ⊂ Q is true.
mcqs.hinglish: Nesting yaad karo: N sabse andar, phir Z, phir Q, sabse bahar R. C options wala direction sahi hai.

traps.A: Negatives are in Z but not N.
traps.B: Fractions like 1/2 are in Q but not Z.
traps.D: Irrationals are in R but not Q - R is bigger.

mcqs.stem: 0.4777... (the 4 not repeating, the 7 repeating) equals:
mcqs.expl: (47 - 4)/90 = 43/90: one 9 for the repeating digit, one 0 for the fixed digit.
mcqs.hinglish: (poora - head)/(9 + 0): (47-4)/90 = 43/90. Option C wala 47/90 hota agar 4 bhi repeat karta.

traps.C: Denominator pattern wrong for mixed recurrence.

mcqs.stem: √2 × √8 equals:
mcqs.hinglish: √2 × √8 = √16 = 4. Under-root multiply hota hai, add nahi.

traps.A: Radicands are multiplied, not added.
traps.C: 2√4 = 4 by luck of notation, but √2·√8 = √16 directly; writing 2√4 shows wrong method.
traps.D: Forgot to take the root at the end.

mcqs.stem: Which is the largest?
mcqs.expl: Squares: 12, 18, 16, 15. The largest square is 18, so 3√2 is largest.
mcqs.hinglish: Sabko square karo: 2√3 → 12, 3√2 → 18, 4 → 16, √15 → 15. Sabse bada square 18 - winner 3√2.

traps.A: 12 is the smallest square here.
traps.D: 15 < 18. Coefficient se confuse hona common galti hai.

mcqs.hinglish: 1/243 ko 3⁻⁵ likho. Negative exponent = reciprocal. x = -5.

traps.D: Equating x with the value, not the exponent.

mcqs.stem: 1/(√5 - 2) equals:
mcqs.expl: Multiply by (√5 + 2): denominator (√5)² - 2² = 5 - 4 = 1. So the value is √5 + 2.
mcqs.hinglish: Conjugate multiply karo, denominator 5-4 = 1 nikla. Answer khud √5+2 hai - magic collapse.

traps.B: That is the original denominator, not the value.

mcqs.hinglish: (a+b)(a-b) = a²-b². Roots ke square = andar wale numbers. 7-5 = 2.

traps.B: Added the squares instead of subtracting.
traps.D: Multiplied radicands - that is √35, a different expression.

mcqs.hinglish: Conjugate multiply karo, denominator 9-8 = 1. Toh 1/x khud conjugate hai. x aur 1/x ka pair yaad rakho.

traps.B: Sign flipped on the wrong term.
traps.D: That is x + 1/x = 6, a different question.

traps.B: Forgot to flip for the negative exponent.
traps.C: Root lene ke baad bhi minus rakh diya - root value negative nahi hoti.

mcqs.hinglish: (a+b)² = a² + 2ab + b². Cross term 2√6 bhoolna sabse common galti. 5 + 2√6.

traps.B: Missed the factor 2 on the cross term.

chapters.name: Algebraic Identities and Factorisation
chapters.title: Chapter 4: Algebraic Identities and Factorisation ★ MOST IMPORTANT
chapters.intro: Pura chapter ek toolbox hai - 8 identities + 5 factorisation moves. Exam mein sabse zyada marks yahin se: near-number evaluation, x+1/x chains, cube bridges aur zero-sum shortcut. Identities ko "kab use karna hai" ke saath yaad karo, akela formula kaam nahi karta.

formulas.meaning: Square + DOUBLE product + square. Beech wala 2ab hi asli identity hai - wo bhool gaye toh sirf squares likhna galat.
Sirf MIDDLE term minus hota hai, last term plus rehta hai. a<sup>2</sup> − 2ab − b<sup>2</sup> likhna classic disaster hai.
Do direction mein chalta hai: factorise karo YA quick multiply karo. "Without direct multiplication" dikhe toh yehi.
x ka coefficient = dono numbers ka SUM, constant = PRODUCT. Sum-product yaad rakhna, expansion nahi karna.
Teen squares + har JODI ka double (3 jodiyan hote hain, bhoolna mat). Cross term ka sign = uske dono parents ke signs ka product.
Signs same order mein: (a+b)<sup>3</sup> sab plus; (a−b)<sup>3</sup> mein + − + − pattern (last term minus!).

formulas.f:
a3 + b3 = (a+b)(a2 − ab + b2)
a3 − b3 = (a−b)(a2 + ab + b2)
formulas.meaning: Bracket apna sign rakhta hai; trinomial ke beech wale term ka sign OPPOSITE. 8a<sup>3</sup>+27b<sup>3</sup> = (2a)<sup>3</sup>+(3b)<sup>3</sup> pehle banao.
a+b aur ab diye ho toh ye bridges DIRECT answer dete hain. Given values kabhi random nahi hote - bridge laga do.
Agar a+b+c = 0 ho toh RIGHT side zero → a3+b3+c3 = 3abc. Ye shortcut exam ka king hai.

formulas.f: x + 1/x = s → x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup> = s<sup>2</sup> − 2 → x<sup>3</sup> + 1/x<sup>3</sup> = s<sup>3</sup> − 3s
formulas.meaning: Chain chalao: har baar square/cube karo aur 2 (ya 3s) minus. x − 1/x = d ho toh PLUS 2 / PLUS 3d hota hai.
Jodi wale identities: difference = 4ab (quick multiply engine), sum = 2(a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>).

formulas.f: Middle-term split: x<sup>2</sup> + px + q → 2 numbers jinka sum p, product q
formulas.meaning: x<sup>2</sup>+7x+12: 4 aur 3 (sum 7, product 12) → (x+4)(x+3). General ax<sup>2</sup>+bx+c mein product = a×c lo.

checks: Golden order of factorisation: (1) HCF common → (2) identity → (3) grouping → (4) middle-term split → (5) substitution. HCF SABSE PEHLE, hamesha.
Near numbers: 982 = (100−2)2, 1033 = (100+3)3, 9992 + 2·999 + 1 = (999+1)2 = 1000000. Round number ke (round ± chhota) mein todo.
Zero-sum instant: a+b+c = 0 dikha → cubes ka sum = 3abc likh ke aage badho. 253 − 753 + 503 = 3×25×(−75)×50.
Crown ka converse: a3+b3+c3 = 3abc ho toh either a+b+c = 0 YA a = b = c.
x4 + x2 + 1 = (x2+x+1)(x2−x+1) - add-subtract x2 trick. x4 − 81 jaise chains mein har layer ko todte raho.
Cubic factoring: x = 1, −1, 2, −2 try karo root ke liye; root mil gaya toh (x − root) se divide.
Sign of cross terms in (a+b+c)2: har cross term ka sign uske dono parents ke signs ka product. Count karo - exactly 3 pairs, har ek twice.
Cube bridge scaled version: 2x+3y = 13, xy = 6 → 8x3+27y3 = (2x+3y)3 − 3(2x)(3y)(2x+3y). Pehle block banao, phir bridge.
Verify karna mana nahi: factorisation ke baad expand karke check karo - 30 second mein galat answer pakda jata hai.

tricks.trick: Near round numbers: 51 × 49 = 50<sup>2</sup> - 1; 102<sup>2</sup> = 100<sup>2</sup> + 2·100·2 + 4
tricks.when: "Evaluate without direct multiplication".

tricks.trick: Given a + b and ab: a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> = (a+b)<sup>2</sup> - 2ab; a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup> = (a+b)<sup>3</sup> - 3ab(a+b)
tricks.when: Bridge questions - the two givens are never random.

tricks.trick: a + b + c = 0 → a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup> + c<sup>3</sup> = 3abc, instantly
tricks.when: Zero-sum cubes like 25<sup>3</sup> - 75<sup>3</sup> + 50<sup>3</sup>.

tricks.trick: x + 1/x = s → square it: x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup> = s<sup>2</sup> - 2 → keep chaining up
tricks.when: The whole x + 1/x family.

tricks.trick: Spot perfect cubes (8, 27, 64, 125, a<sup>3</sup>b<sup>3</sup>) → apply a<sup>3</sup> ± b<sup>3</sup>
tricks.when: 27a<sup>3</sup> + 64 type expressions.

tricks.trick: Cubic factoring: test x = 1, -1, 2, -2 for a root, then divide
tricks.when: x<sup>3</sup> - 3x<sup>2</sup> - 9x - 5 type.

tricks.trick: HCF first, ALWAYS - before any identity or grouping
tricks.when: Every factorisation: move 1 of the golden sequence.

imps.stem: Evaluate using identities: (i) 102², (ii) 98², (iii) 9.7².
steps: Given: three squares near round numbers. Write each as (100 ± k) or (10 ± k).
why: The identity replaces one hard multiplication with three easy pieces; the cross term 2×100×k does the heavy lifting.
imps.hinglish: Round number ke paas wale squares ka JUGAAD: (100±2)². 98² = 10000 - 400 + 4 = 9604. Dhyan do: 9.7² mein cross term 2×10×0.3 = 6, aur 0.3² = 0.09 - decimals ka square chhota hota hai, 0.9 nahi!

imps.stem: If a + b = 10 and a - b = 4, find (i) a² + b² and (ii) ab - all in one line each, using identities.
steps: Given: the pair-sum and pair-difference. Needed: sum of squares and the product.
Add the two squares identities: (a+b)² + (a-b)² = 2(a² + b²).
Check: (a+b)(a-b) = 10×4 = 40 = a² - b²; with a²+b² = 58 we get a² = 49, b² = 9, a = 7, b = 3 ✓ (ab = 21 ✓).
why: The two companion identities convert (a+b, a-b) directly into (a²+b², ab) without ever solving for a and b.
imps.hinglish: Ye identity-pair exam ka shortcut bomb hai: (a+b)²+(a-b)² = 2(a²+b²) aur (a+b)²-(a-b)² = 4ab. Dono values plug karo - 58 aur 21. Solving for a, b optional hai, sirf check ke liye.

imps.stem: Factorise: (i) x² + 7x + 12, (ii) x² - 5x - 36, (iii) x² - 11x + 24.
steps: Given: three monic quadratics. Find two numbers with the right SUM and PRODUCT.
why: Expanding (x+p)(x+q) gives sum and product - so factorising reverses exactly those two readings.
imps.hinglish: Do numbers dhoondo: jiska sum middle coefficient ho, product last term ho. Sign logic: product positive toh dono same sign (sum ke hisaab se), product negative toh alag-alag. (ii) mein product -36 aur sum -5: -9 aur +4 jeette hain.

imps.stem: If x + 1/x = 5, find (i) x² + 1/x² and (ii) x⁴ + 1/x⁴.
steps: Given: x + 1/x = 5. Square both sides: x² + 2 + 1/x² = 25.
why: Every square introduces a constant middle term 2 (because x · 1/x = 1); subtract it to keep the chain clean.
imps.hinglish: Chain method: square karo, 2 minus karo, phir dobara square karo, phir 2 minus. 5 → 23 → 527. Ek hi line mein: (x+1/x)² - 2 = x²+1/x². Ye chain chalti hi jati hai - x⁶ ke liye x³ wale bridge ka use hota hai.

imps.stem: If a + b = 12 and ab = 27, find a³ + b³ and a² + b².
steps: Given: pair-sum and product. Cube bridge: a³ + b³ = (a+b)³ - 3ab(a+b).
why: Both bridges express symmetric quantities in terms of (sum, product) - no need to solve for a and b.
imps.hinglish: Symmetric quantities ka rule: sab kuch (sum, product) se nikhlo. Cube bridge: (a+b)³ - 3ab(a+b). 1728 - 972 = 756. Square: 144 - 54 = 90. Solving a, b se bhi hoga but identity wala path 2 line ka hai.

imps.stem: Using a suitable identity, evaluate 12³ + 1³ + (-13)³.
steps: Zero-sum shortcut: if a + b + c = 0 then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.
why: The identity a³+b³+c³-3abc = (a+b+c)(...) collapses to 0 on the left whenever a+b+c = 0.
imps.hinglish: Numbers dekho: 12, 1, -13 - sum zero! Turant shortcut: cubes ka sum = 3abc = -468. Bina koi cube nikaale. Ye 'zero-sum spotting' exam mein 3 second ka kaam hai - 5 marks bachate hain.

imps.stem: Factorise completely: x³ - 3x² - 9x - 5.
steps: Hunt for an integer root: try x = -1: (-1)³ - 3(1) - 9(-1) - 5 = -1 - 3 + 9 - 5 = 0 ✓. So (x + 1) is a factor.
Factorise the quadratic: x² - 4x - 5: sum -4, product -5 → -5 and +1: (x - 5)(x + 1).
why: An integer root r of a polynomial always yields the factor (x - r); testing small integers (0, ±1, ±2) is the fastest opening move.
imps.hinglish: Cubic factorisation ka opening: chhote integers try karo. x = -1 par zero mila, toh (x+1) factor. Long division ya coefficient comparison se quadratic mila: x²-4x-5, wo phir middle-term split. Final (x+1)²(x-5).

imps.stem: If x + y + z = 6 and xy + yz + zx = 11, find x³ + y³ + z³ - 3xyz.
steps: First get the sum of squares: x²+y²+z² = (x+y+z)² - 2(xy+yz+zx) = 36 - 22 = 14.
Crown identity: x³+y³+z³-3xyz = (x+y+z)(x²+y²+z² - xy - yz - zx).
why: The crown identity needs (sum) and (sum of squares minus pair-sum) - both computable from the givens.
imps.hinglish: Do steps: pehle x²+y²+z² = 36-22 = 14. Phir crown identity: bracket = 14-11 = 3. Multiply: 6×3 = 18. Zero-sum nahi tha isliye poora identity use hua.

imps.stem: If 9x² + 25y² = 181 and xy = 2, find 3x - 5y.
why: Spotting the scaled square (3x, 5y) converts the given sum of squares into a completed square minus the cross term.
imps.hinglish: 9x² aur 25y² ko (3x)², (5y)² dekho. Cross term 2×3x×5y = 30xy = 60. 181 - 60 = 121 = 11². Sign: dono values possible - ±11. Ye 'scaled variables' wala pattern har identity mein chalta hai.

imps.stem: Without cubing any number, evaluate 25³ - 75³ + 50³.
why: The zero sum makes three cubes collapse into one product - this is the identity's designed use.
imps.hinglish: 25 - 75 + 50 = 0 - zero-sum! -75 ko b banake shortcut lagao: 3×25×(-75)×50 = -281250. Teen cubes (15625 + ... + 125000) karne ki zaroorat hi nahi. Sign: ek negative factor, toh result negative.

imps.stem: Without cubing, evaluate 0.86³ + 0.14³.
why: The pair-sum 1 makes (a+b)³ trivial; only the product needs one multiplication.
imps.hinglish: 0.86 + 0.14 = 1 - yahi design hai. Bridge: 1 - 3(0.1204) = 0.6388. Decimals ka product dhyan se: 86×14 = 1204, four decimal places. Cubes bilkul nahi nikaale.

imps.stem: If p³ + q³ = 35 and p + q = 5, find pq.
why: The bridge reads equally well backwards: the product is recovered from the two cube-related quantities.
imps.hinglish: Bridge ka reverse use: 35 = 125 - 15pq. pq = 6. Check: p, q roots of t²-5t+6 = (t-2)(t-3): p=2, q=3 → 8+27 = 35 ✓.

chapters.name: Perimeter and Area
chapters.title: Chapter 6: Perimeter and Area ★ MOST IMPORTANT
chapters.intro: Book ka sabse scoring chapter - Heron, circles, sectors, rings aur composite figures. Ek hi baat yaad rakho: figure banao (2 inch ka bhi), values likho, phir formula fire karo. π ka choice (22/7 vs 3.14) pehla decision hai har circle question ka.

formulas.f:
Rectangle: P = 2(l + b), A = l × b
Square: P = 4a, A = a2, diagonal = a√2
formulas.meaning: Basic shapes. Square ka diagonal side ka √2 guna - reverse mein bhi use hota hai.
Height base ke PERPENDICULAR honi chahiye. Parallelogram ka aadha hota hai same base-height pe.
Teen sides diye ho toh yehi. Rhythm: s nikalo → 3 differences → multiply (pair smart) → root.

formulas.f: Right triangle? A = ½ × leg × leg (Heron SKIP)
formulas.meaning: Sides 5-12-13, 9-40-41 jaise dikhe (a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>=c<sup>2</sup>) toh right angle hai - direct formula, time bachao.
Sab sides barabar? Heron ki zaroorat nahi. Reverse bhi: area diya ho toh side = √(4A/√3).

formulas.f:
Parallelogram: A = b×h
Rhombus: A = ½d1d2
Trapezium: A = ½(a+b)h
formulas.meaning: Rhombus mein DIAGNALS (perpendicular) ka product aadha. Trapezium mein parallel sides ka sum, height, aadha.
π ka choice: radius 7 ka multiple ho toh 22/7, warna 3.14. Reverse: C diya → r = C/(2π).

formulas.f:
Arc: ℓ = (θ/360) × 2πr
Sector area: (θ/360) × πr2 = ½ℓr
Sector perimeter = ℓ + 2r
formulas.meaning: Sector = pizza slice: poore circle ka θ/360 hissa. Gem: A = ½ × arc × r. Perimeter mein DONO radii + arc.
Chord aur arc ke beech ka hissa. Sector se equilateral/60° triangle minus karo (θ=60° pe triangle equilateral hota hai).

formulas.f:
Ring: A = π(R2 − r2) = π(R+r)(R−r)
Outside path: R = r + w
formulas.meaning: Donut ka area. Path bahar ho toh outer radius = inner + width; path andar ho toh radii minus karo.
Kitne chakkar = kitni distance / circumference. Reverse bhi chalta hai.
Char sides wala CYCLIC quadrilateral (sab vertices circle par). Same s = semi-perimeter; koi (s−..) multiply hota hai.
formulas.ex: s = 31, sides 13,14,15,20 type → root before multiply

formulas.meaning: Bade field ka unit. hectare → m<sup>2</sup> mein x10000.

checks: Heron mein pairing smart karo: (s−a)(s−b)(s−c) ko aise jodo ki multiplication easy ho - jaise 18×7×11×4 ko (18×4)×(7×11).
Wire re-bending questions: perimeter SAME rehta hai - pehle shape ka perimeter nikaalo, wahi naye shape ka radius/side banta hai.
Ratio questions: sides ko 3x, 4x, 5x likho, perimeter/x diya hua use karke x nikaalo, phir Heron.
Composite figures: rectangle + semicircle, circle in square - area ko TODDO (add ya minus), perimeter ko TRACE karo (sirf outer boundary).
Ring ke 2 givens: (R−r) aur (R+r) alag alag diye ho toh direct (R+r)(R−r) multiply karo - individual radii ki zaroorat nahi.
Chord wala ring trick: chord of OUTER circle tangent to inner → half-chord2 = R2 − r2 (Pythagoras) → ring area = π × (chord/2)2.
Goat/cow grazing: corner pe tied → sector of angle 90°; edge ke beech mein → 180°. Sector area = fraction of circle.
Track questions: perimeter = 2 straights + 1 full circle (2 semicircles); area = rectangle + full circle.
Same perimeter different shapes: circle ka area SABSE BADA hota hai - comparison MCQs ka standard answer.
Units discipline: cm vs m vs km - pehle same unit mein lao, phir formula. Answer ke saath unit likhna compulsory hai.

tricks.trick: π choice: radius multiple of 7 → 22/7; otherwise 3.14
tricks.when: First decision of every circle question.

tricks.trick: Sector and arc = θ/360 × (full circle value). Gem: sector area = ½ × arc × r
tricks.when: Pizza-slice sector questions.

tricks.trick: Sides satisfy a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> = c<sup>2</sup>? Area = ½ × leg × leg - skip Heron
tricks.when: 5-12-13, 9-40-41 style triangles.

tricks.trick: Heron rhythm: s → three differences → multiply (pair smartly) → root
tricks.when: Three sides given, height unknown.

tricks.trick: Ring: A = π(R+r)(R-r). Path outside: R = r + w. Path inside: subtract squares
tricks.when: Garden path / ring / border questions.

tricks.trick: Wheel: distance = revolutions × circumference
tricks.when: "How many revolutions / how far does it travel".

tricks.trick: Equilateral: area = (√3/4)a<sup>2</sup>, height = (√3/2)a
tricks.when: All sides equal - no Heron needed.

imps.stem: Find the area of a triangle with sides 5 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm.
steps: Differences: s - a = 10, s - b = 3, s - c = 2.
Cross-check: 5² + 12² = 169 = 13², so it is right-angled; ½ × 5 × 12 = 30 ✓.
why: Spotting the right angle gives an instant verification - Heron must agree with ½ab.
imps.hinglish: Heron ka 4-step rhythm: s nikaalo, differences nikaalo, multiply, root. 15×10×3×2 = 900, root = 30. Bonus: 5-12-13 Pythagorean triple hai - ½×5×12 = 30 se confirm.

imps.stem: For a circle of radius 7 cm, find (i) the length of an arc subtending 90° at the centre and (ii) the area of the corresponding sector.
why: Everything scales by θ/360 - compute the full-circle value once, then take the fraction.
imps.hinglish: 90° matlab quarter circle. Arc = 44/4 = 11 cm, area = 154/4 = 38.5 cm². Fraction pehle likho, calculation aadhi ho jati hai.

imps.stem: Two concentric circles have radii 10 cm and 6 cm. Find the area of the ring between them (π = 3.14).
why: Subtract the inner disk from the outer disk; factorising R²-r² = (R+r)(R-r) speeds the arithmetic.
imps.hinglish: Ring = bada circle - chhota circle. π(100-36) = 64π. 3.14 se: 200.96 cm². R²-r² ko (R+r)(R-r) likhoge toh mental math ho jata hai.

imps.stem: A triangular park has sides 122 m, 120 m and 22 m. Find its area.
why: Pair the factors smartly: 132×110 = 14520 and 10×12 = 120; 14520×120 = 1742400. Grouping reveals the square: (1320)².
imps.hinglish: s = 132, differences 10, 12, 110. Product 1742400, root 1320 m². Note the beauty: root = s × 10 = 1320 - aise patterns pehchano.

imps.stem: A cyclic quadrilateral has sides 13 cm, 10 cm, 13 cm and 10 cm (in order). Find its area using Brahmagupta's formula.
why: Heron's pattern extends to four sides; the symmetric sides make every difference reappear - a designed clean answer.
imps.hinglish: Cyclic quadrilateral mein Heron ka bhai Brahmagupta: same (s - side) pattern, char baar. s = 23, differences 10,13,10,13. Product 16900, root 130 cm².

imps.stem: A wheel of diameter 70 cm makes a journey of 1.1 km. How many complete revolutions does it make (π = 22/7)?
steps: Convert the journey: 1.1 km = 1100 m = 110000 cm.
why: One revolution moves the wheel exactly one circumference; total distance divided by circumference gives the count.
imps.hinglish: Ek chakkar = circumference = 220 cm. Distance 110000 cm. 110000/220 = 500 revolutions. Units same karo pehle - km vs cm sabse common galti.

imps.stem: A sector of a circle of radius 21 cm has central angle 120°. Find (i) the arc length, (ii) the sector area, (iii) the sector's perimeter.
steps: Full circle: C = 2π(21) = 132 cm; A = π(441) = 1386 cm².
imps.answer: arc 44 cm; area 462 cm²; perimeter 86 cm
why: The sector owns one third of the circumference AND one third of the area; its perimeter needs the two straight edges too.
imps.hinglish: 120° = one-third. Arc 44, area 462. Perimeter mein DO radii: 44 + 42 = 86 cm. Arc + ek radius likhna classic mistake hai.

imps.stem: A wire of length 132 cm is first bent into an equilateral triangle and then re-bent into a circle. Which shape encloses more area, and by how much (√3 ≈ 1.73, π = 22/7)?
imps.answer: Circle: 1386 vs 484√3 ≈ 837.3; the circle encloses about 548.7 cm² more.
why: The same perimeter always encloses more area as a circle than as any polygon - this question quantifies it.
imps.hinglish: Same wire, do shapes. Triangle: 484√3 ≈ 837 cm². Circle: 1386 cm². Circle 549 cm² zyada. Ye universal truth hai - fixed perimeter par circle sabse bada area deta hai.

imps.stem: A circular park of radius 17 m is surrounded by a path 4 m wide running outside it. Find the area of the path (π = 22/7).
why: An outside path adds to the radius once; the ring formula πw(2r + w) is the fast version: (22/7)(4)(38).
imps.hinglish: Bahar wala path: R = 21. π(152) ≈ 477.7 m². Shortcut: πw(2r+w) = (22/7)×4×38 - same answer, direct.

imps.stem: A running track is 90 m long on each straight and has two semicircular ends of diameter 56 m. Find (i) the perimeter of the track and (ii) the area enclosed (π = 22/7).
steps: Perimeter = two straights + two semicircular arcs = 90 + 90 + one full circle of diameter 56.
why: Two semicircles of equal diameter combine into one full circle - for both length and area.
imps.hinglish: Do semicircles = ek full circle. Perimeter 180 + 176 = 356 m. Area 5040 + 2464 = 7504 m². Track problems mein halves ko jod kar full banao.

imps.stem: A circular garden has radius 35 m. Fencing costs ₹20 per metre and ploughing costs ₹0.50 per m². Find the total cost of fencing the boundary once and ploughing the whole garden (π = 22/7).
why: Perimeter multiplies per-metre rates; area multiplies per-square-metre rates - never interchange them.
imps.hinglish: Fencing = boundary × rate/m: 220×20 = 4400. Ploughing = area × rate/m²: 3850×0.5 = 1925. Total ₹6325. Rate ke saath unit dekho - /m ya /m².

imps.stem: A goat is tied to one corner of a rectangular field 40 m by 30 m with a rope 21 m long. Find the area it can graze, assuming it cannot leave the field (π = 22/7).
steps: At a corner of a rectangle, only 90° of the circle's sweep lies inside the field: a quarter circle.
why: The two fences of the corner cut the reachable disk to a quarter; the rope length is the radius.
imps.hinglish: Corner par sirf 90° ka sector available - quarter circle. ¼ × π × 441 = 346.5 m². Rope = radius, corner = center.

mcqs.hinglish: 2(15+8) = 46 aur 15×8 = 120. Units: cm aur cm².

mcqs.hinglish: 147π = 462. Difference of squares.

mcqs.hinglish: One-third of circumference.
